nodes.title: Chain-first verify blobs hard-code `anchored: true` and drop anchoring's status/acknowledged, so a 'submitting' or failed anchor reads isAnchored: true (v1 + v2)
nodes.description:
## BLUF

**The chain-first verify branches build their blockchain blob with** `anchored: true` **hard-coded and no** `status`**, which makes the honest-anchor guard** `settled` **BY CONSTRUCTION.** An anchoring reply that is still in flight or has failed — `status: 'submitting'`, `acknowledged: false`, the KS-726 class — is therefore presented as `isAnchored: true`, in both the v1 and the v2 verify routes.

The code says so itself. `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:130-132`:

> *"KS-1628: a failed anchor is not an anchor, whatever else the blob says. The chain-first blobs carry* `anchored: true` *and no status, so they are unaffected; a stored blob that pairs* `anchored: true` *with a failed status was on-chain before this line."*

That comment reads as a reassurance. It is in fact the statement of the defect: *unaffected by the failed-status guard* is exactly the problem, because the guard is the thing that would have caught this.

Gate O1's Minor 2 on the twelve-PR batch, 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z. Pre-existing; not in those merges.

## The mechanism, measured

`isAnchoredHonestly` (`verification.ts:120`) decides the claim:

```ts
if (FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(c.status))) return false;   // :133
const settled = c.anchored === true || c.status === 'confirmed';  // :141
```

* A **real stored** anchor row has no `anchored` boolean at all — the comment at `:136-139` says so: *"anchoring's vocabulary is pending | submitted | confirmed | failed … and there is NO* `anchored` *boolean on a real row."* For those rows only `status === 'confirmed'` earns the claim, and `'submitted'` deliberately does not, because *"the tx is in flight and may still fail — the KS-535 class."*
* A **chain-first** blob is built by hand with `anchored: true` and **no** `status` **key**. So `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES.has(String(undefined))` is false — the failed guard cannot fire — and `settled` is true on the first disjunct, whatever anchoring actually reported.

**The four construction sites:**

| route | site |
| -- | -- |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:717` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1237` |
| v1 | `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:1259` |
| **v2** | `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:233`, inside `chainOnlyMatch` |

The `status` argument the call sites pass does not rescue it: `verification.ts:758`, `:1297` and `verificationV2.ts:271` pass the **literal** `'anchored'`, and in any case the second argument is only consulted when there is no chain blob at all (`:149`).

**What bounds the severity.** `settled` is necessary but not sufficient: the claim also needs `typeof c.txHash === 'string'`, `REAL_TXHASH_RE` (64 hex) and `heightOk`. So the hash must already look like a real one, and it comes from the chain index. The defect is that **in-flight and failed anchors the index knows about still read as anchored** — not that an arbitrary blob does.

## Why High

On a document-authenticity platform, `isAnchored: true` is the product's central claim to a verifier. Presenting a `'submitting'` or failed anchor as anchored is the same family as KS-535 (a failed on-chain anchor reporting `status: anchored`) and KS-1634 (a simulated anchor returned unlabelled), and KS-1634 is High. The failure direction is always *over*-claiming, never under-claiming.

**Honest limit on this rating: I did not run a census.** I have not measured how many rows can reach these branches with a non-confirmed status today. The nearest evidence is KS-1634's census — 0 qualifying rows on both boxes at 2026-10-18, with kintsugi's 0 noted as contingent on one document row — and that census was for a different precondition. **A census is the first step on this ticket, and the rating should be revisited against it.**

## Recommendation

1. Carry anchoring's own fields into the chain-first blob instead of asserting the conclusion: pass `status` and `acknowledged` through, and let `isAnchoredHonestly` apply the same rules it applies to a stored row. Dropping `anchored: true` entirely is the cleaner shape, since no real row carries it — but `ks563` pins the current chain-first shape, so that is a deliberate change with a test to re-cut, not a one-liner.
2. A cell per site: a chain-first match whose anchoring status is `'submitting'` (and one that is `'failed'`) must read `isAnchored: false`. A mutant restoring the hard-coded `anchored: true` must red each of them.
3. Fold the **v2** site in with KS-1634's v2 work — it is the same four lines of construction, and splitting them across two tickets invites one to be done and the other forgotten.

## Dedupe

Over all **1,627** Secuura-PK issues including archived: `chainOnlyMatch` **→ 0 hits.** `anchored: true` → 4, each a different subject (KS-1634 the simulated-label defect, KS-1628 the route retirement, KS-834 a decision on verify auth, KS-535 the document-status variant, Done). `acknowledged` → 6, none about this presenter. `isAnchored` → 9; the nearest, KS-1637, is gate N1's residue about the removal pin reading only the router — a different mechanism, read and confirmed distinct. Positive controls on the same corpus: `verification` 360, `anchor` 313. Zero control: a nonsense token reads 0.

**Related:** KS-1634 (the same presenter, the `simulated` signal, and the v2 site it shares), KS-726 (the `status: 'submitting'` / `acknowledged: false` reply class this mis-presents; Done), KS-535 (the document-status variant; Done), KS-563 (which pins the current chain-first shape, so its cells are in scope for any change here).

---

*Filed by Seat R 51st on Wednesday's instruction of 2026-10-19T01:00:25Z, citing gate O1's verdict section "Minor 2". The Linear actor field is shared across the fleet, so authorship is this line, not the actor. Everything above the "Why High" section I verified in the source at develop* `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`*; the severity and the census limit are my own call, stated as such. Not fixed in these merges.*
